$comment: This file holds POLICY (which layer may depend on which) and DATA (lists of
headers and symbols). It deliberately does not hold MECHANISM: comment
stripping, the fail-closed header classifier and cycle detection stay in the
checker so that no edit to this file can switch them off.
Editing rules here is a reviewed change, and tests/python/test_architecture.py
re-reads this file to assert the non-negotiable architecture propositions
(see 'immutable_propositions' below). A rule edit that violates them fails CI.
Layer names are top-level directories under src/, except that a layer with
sub-directories (backend, bindings) also gets one entry per sub-directory, so

core.reason: Platform-neutral native types. Must not know about any OS or the Python runtime.

platform.reason: Thin native file and error primitives shared by every backend.

backend.reason: Backend dispatch: registration and the public entry points.

bindings/python.reason: The only component allowed to include Python.h or nanobind. Composition root.

discover.reason: Runtime probing. Reports capability values upward; does not select backends.

diagnostics.reason: Logging, integrity checking and allocation tracking.

$comment_namespace_exemptions: Every entry is {path, reason}. A bare path is rejected: an exemption whose
reason is not written down becomes an unreviewable precedent, and the next
contributor has no way to judge whether their case is the same.
An exemption states that the CHECKER cannot express the rule for this file --
not that the architecture may bend here. A file that needs an exemption because
it genuinely lives outside the layering is a broken design; fix the design, not

namespace_exemptions.reason: NB_MODULE() is nanobind's module bootstrap and must expand at global scope; the binding generator does not allow wrapping it in a namespace.
The header contains only preprocessor macros (UR_LOG and friends) and declares no entities, so the 'file declares a namespace' rule does not apply.

$comment_dependencies: Each entry lists the components its key may include. '_self' expands to every
component in the same top-level layer (backend/linux may include backend/macos's
public headers but the reverse coupling is what gets caught).
Every component must appear as a key: a typo in a layer name fails the run
instead of silently dropping a rule.

core.reason: core is the bottom of the stack; anything above it would invert the layers.

platform.reason: Platform primitives wrap OS calls and store them opaquely; they may not reach upward.

backend.reason: Dispatch layer may see everything below it plus its own implementations.

backend/linux.reason: One OS implementation; sees the shared core, never another backend's internals.

backend/macos.reason: One OS implementation; sees the shared core, never another backend's internals.

backend/thread.reason: Portable implementation; sees the shared core and platform primitives.

backend/windows.reason: One OS implementation; sees the shared core, never another backend's internals.

bindings/python.reason: Composition root. It surfaces backend-specific knobs (set_iocp_worker_count, quarantine_stats) to Python. That it must not grow dispatch logic is a semantic rule no include graph can decide, so review covers it.

discover.reason: Probing reports capability values upward. Backend selection belongs to core::BackendRegistry (docs/architecture.md), so discovery must not know concrete backends -- which would also form a cycle with backend -> discover.

diagnostics.reason: Diagnostics depends on core; never the other way around.

$comment_platform_headers: One entry per top-level layer. Sub-directories inherit their parent's entry.
Any header the classifier judges non-standard is rejected in a layer absent here.
$comment_native_symbols: Only TYPES belong here. 'io_uring' is intentionally absent: it appears in core
as a backend-name string and as config fields (io_uring_queue_depth), both of
which are platform-neutral. Restricting the list to types keeps the check about
architecture rather than about work the compiler already does.
$comment_immutable: Non-negotiable propositions. tests/python/test_architecture.py reads this file
and asserts every one of them still holds, so a rule edit cannot quietly loosen
the architecture. Add to this list deliberately; do not remove entries.

immutable_propositions.description: core may not depend on platform, any backend, discover, or bindings.
core may not include any non-standard header.
bindings/python is the top of the stack; no layer may include it.
diagnostics may only depend on core and itself.
discovery must not know concrete backends.
One OS implementation must not include another's private headers.
